entries.desc: Norman victory over the Byzantine Empire on the Adriatic coast that opened Robert Guiscard's campaign into the Balkans.
entries.tldr: On 18 October 1081, Norman forces under Robert Guiscard defeated a Byzantine army led by Emperor Alexios I Komnenos outside the Adriatic port of Dyrrhachium, after the elite Varangian Guard, many of them English exiles, was lured into a fatal pursuit. The emperor's daughter Anna Komnene later gave a detailed account of the battle in her Alexiad. The victory let the Normans open a campaign deep into the Byzantine Balkans, though troubles in Italy eventually forced Guiscard to abandon it.

entries.name: Akkerman Convention
entries.desc: Treaty between the Russian and Ottoman Empires settling disputes over Serbia and the Danubian Principalities.
entries.tldr: Signed in October 1826 in the Bessarabian town of Akkerman, this convention between the Russian and Ottoman empires resolved disputes left unsettled by the 1812 Treaty of Bucharest. It confirmed Serbia's autonomy under Ottoman suzerainty and expanded Russian influence over the Danubian Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia. Russia extracted the concessions under threat of renewed war while the Ottomans were busy suppressing the Greek War of Independence. It failed to prevent a fresh Russo-Turkish war two years later.

entries.name: Battle of Megiddo
entries.desc: Decisive British-led offensive in Palestine that shattered Ottoman forces and hastened the empire's collapse.

entries.name: Battle of Manzikert
entries.desc: Seljuk victory over the Byzantine Empire that opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

entries.name: Battle of Jaffa
entries.desc: Richard the Lionheart's defense of Jaffa against Saladin during the Third Crusade.

entries.name: Battle of Vienna
entries.desc: Coalition victory that broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna and halted Ottoman expansion into Central Europe.

entries.name: Armenian–Azerbaijani War
entries.desc: Territorial conflict between the newly independent Armenian and Azerbaijani republics after the Russian Empire's collapse.
entries.tldr: After the Russian Empire's collapse in 1917–1918, the newly independent Democratic Republic of Armenia and Azerbaijan Democratic Republic fought over contested, ethnically mixed territories including Nagorno-Karabakh, Nakhchivan, and Zangezur. Both fledgling states waged intermittent fighting alongside massacres of civilians on both sides between 1918 and 1920. The conflict ended only when the Soviet Red Army invaded and absorbed both republics, imposing borders that left unresolved grievances over Karabakh.

entries.name: Battle of Poitiers
entries.desc: Major English victory during the Hundred Years' War in which King John II of France was captured.

entries.name: Night attack at Târgoviște
entries.desc: Surprise nighttime assault by Vlad the Impaler on the Ottoman army encamped in Wallachia.

entries.name: Operation Faustschlag
entries.desc: German offensive against Soviet Russia that forced the Bolsheviks to accept the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk.

entries.name: Battle of Chains
entries.desc: Early Rashidun victory under Khalid ibn al-Walid over Sasanian forces in Mesopotamia.
entries.tldr: Fought in 633 CE in lower Mesopotamia, the battle was among the earliest engagements of the Muslim conquest of Persia, as the Rashidun general Khalid ibn al-Walid led an Arab army against Sasanian Persian forces defending the frontier near the Euphrates. Tradition holds the battle's name comes from the Persian practice of chaining soldiers together in ranks to prevent retreat, a tactic that instead trapped many defenders when their lines broke. Khalid's decisive victory opened the path for further Muslim advances that steadily eroded Persian control of Mesopotamia.

entries.name: Battle of Stamford Bridge
entries.desc: King Harold II's victory over Norwegian invaders in England, ending Viking claims to the English throne.

entries.name: Battle of Plassey
entries.desc: British East India Company victory over the Nawab of Bengal that established British colonial control in India.

entries.name: Battle of Hannut
entries.desc: A major tank battle in Belgium during the German invasion of the Low Countries, one of the largest armored clashes of the early war.
entries.tldr: Fought on 12–13 May 1940 in Belgium, this clash between the French Cavalry Corps under General René Prioux and two German panzer divisions was, at the time, the largest tank battle in history. French Somua and Hotchkiss tanks inflicted heavier losses on the German armor and arguably won on tactical terms, buying time for Allied forces further west. The engagement proved strategically irrelevant, though, since the main German thrust drove through the lightly defended Ardennes further south.

entries.name: Italo-Turkish War
entries.desc: Italy seized the Ottoman provinces of Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, forming the colony of Libya and marking the first military use of aircraft.

entries.name: Battle of Wuhan
entries.desc: One of the largest battles of the Second Sino-Japanese War, fought over the strategic tri-city area of Wuhan in central China.

entries.name: Battle of Tampere
entries.desc: A decisive battle of the Finnish Civil War in which White forces captured the Red stronghold of Tampere.

entries.name: Kellogg-Briand pact
entries.desc: An international agreement, signed in Paris, in which signatory states renounced war as an instrument of national policy.

entries.name: Battle of Breitenfeld
entries.desc: A decisive Swedish and Saxon victory over Catholic League forces during the Thirty Years' War, marking Sweden's emergence as a major power.
entries.tldr: Fought on 17 September 1631 near Leipzig, the battle marked a turning point in the Thirty Years' War as the Protestant army of King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden, allied with Saxon forces, decisively defeated the Catholic League army under Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly. Gustavus Adolphus's flexible infantry formations and mobile artillery overcame the collapse of the inexperienced Saxon wing to rout Tilly's veterans. Sweden's first major battle on German soil shattered the Catholic League's reputation for invincibility and opened much of Germany to Swedish advance.

entries.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
entries.desc: Lakota, Cheyenne, and Arapaho forces led by Crazy Horse and Sitting Bull annihilated Custer's 7th Cavalry detachment in Montana.

entries.name: Battle of the Bridge
entries.desc: A rare early defeat for the Rashidun Caliphate's forces, routed by a Sasanian army after crossing the Euphrates on a pontoon bridge.

entries.name: French Revolutionary Wars
entries.desc: A series of conflicts between Revolutionary France and a coalition of European monarchies seeking to contain and reverse the Revolution.

entries.name: Siege of Fort William Henry
entries.desc: French and Native American forces besieged and captured a British fort in colonial New York during the French and Indian War.

entries.name: Lazic War
entries.desc: A protracted conflict between the Byzantine and Sasanian empires for control of Lazica, on the eastern Black Sea coast.

entries.name: Battle of Dunkirk
entries.desc: German forces trapped Allied troops on the French coast, prompting a large-scale evacuation across the English Channel.
entries.tldr: In late May and early June 1940, German panzer divisions pushed British and French forces back to the Channel port of Dunkirk during the Battle of France, threatening to trap the entire British Expeditionary Force. A controversial German halt order and fierce Allied rearguard resistance bought time for Operation Dynamo, in which destroyers and civilian 'little ships' ferried roughly 338,000 troops to England. Though a military defeat with vast equipment losses, the rescue was recast in Britain as a defiant 'Dunkirk spirit' that stiffened resolve to keep fighting.

entries.name: Battle of Mactan
entries.desc: Filipino chieftain Lapu-Lapu's warriors repelled a Spanish expedition and killed explorer Ferdinand Magellan on Mactan Island.

entries.name: Mongol invasions and conquests
entries.desc: Beginning under Genghis Khan in Mongolia, Mongol armies built the largest contiguous land empire in history, stretching across Asia and into Europe.

entries.name: Eighth Russo-Turkish War
entries.desc: A war between the Russian and Ottoman empires over Balkan and Black Sea territories, ending with the Treaty of Bucharest.

entries.name: Battle of Ankara
entries.desc: Timur's forces decisively defeated and captured the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I, plunging the Ottoman Empire into a period of civil war.
entries.tldr: On 20 July 1402, the Central Asian conqueror Timur led his army against the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I near Ankara, a clash between two rival powers seeking regional dominance. Bayezid's forces, weakened by defections from resentful Anatolian vassals, were encircled and shattered, and the sultan was captured, reportedly dying in captivity within a year. The catastrophe threw the young Ottoman state into a decade-long civil war among Bayezid's sons. Timur, uninterested in permanent conquest, withdrew eastward, unintentionally giving the Ottomans time to recover.

entries.name: Battle of Kulikovo
entries.desc: A coalition of Russian principalities led by Dmitri Donskoi defeated the Golden Horde, a turning point in Russian resistance to Mongol rule.

entries.name: Montevideo Convention
entries.desc: A treaty signed in Montevideo, Uruguay, codifying the widely cited criteria for statehood in international law.

entries.name: Sykes–Picot Agreement
entries.desc: A secret Anglo-French agreement that divided the Ottoman Empire's Arab provinces into spheres of influence, shaping the modern Middle East.

entries.name: Battle of Nicopolis
entries.desc: An Ottoman army under Bayezid I crushed a large European crusading force near the Danube, ending hopes of relieving Christian rule in the Balkans.

entries.name: War of the Polish Succession
entries.desc: A European conflict over the Polish throne, fought mainly in Italy and the Rhineland, pitting France and Spain against Austria and Russia.

entries.name: Philippine–American War
entries.desc: An armed conflict between the First Philippine Republic and the United States following the Spanish-American War, resulting in American colonial rule of the islands.

entries.name: Turkish Abductions
entries.desc: Barbary corsairs from North Africa raided Iceland, killing dozens and carrying several hundred captives into slavery in Algiers.

entries.name: Second Boer War
entries.desc: A war between the British Empire and the Boer republics of the Transvaal and Orange Free State for control of southern Africa's goldfields.

entries.name: Union of Utrecht
entries.desc: An alliance of northern Dutch provinces against Spanish rule that laid the constitutional foundation for the Dutch Republic.

entries.name: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
entries.desc: An international agreement establishing mutual recognition of copyright between signatory nations, negotiated in Berne, Switzerland.

entries.name: Marco Polo Bridge incident
entries.desc: A clash between Chinese and Japanese troops near Beijing that escalated into full-scale war between China and Japan.

entries.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
entries.desc: A coalition of Christian Iberian kingdoms decisively defeated the Almohad Caliphate, a turning point in the Reconquista.

entries.name: Soviet–Japanese War
entries.desc: The Soviet Union's invasion of Japanese-held Manchuria, Korea, and the Kuril Islands in the final days of World War II.

entries.name: First Battle of Bull Run
entries.desc: The first major land battle of the American Civil War, ending in a Confederate victory near Manassas, Virginia.

entries.name: Treaty of the Pyrenees
entries.desc: A peace treaty ending the Franco-Spanish War and establishing the modern border between France and Spain along the Pyrenees.

entries.name: Battle of the Ardennes
entries.desc: An early clash of World War I in which French and German armies fought inconclusively in the forested Ardennes region.

entries.name: War of the Quadruple Alliance
entries.desc: Britain, France, Austria, and the Dutch Republic united to check Spanish expansion in Italy under Cardinal Alberoni's foreign policy.

entries.name: Brusilov Offensive
entries.desc: A massive Russian offensive against Austro-Hungarian forces on the Eastern Front, one of the most successful Allied operations of World War I.

entries.name: Battle of Bosworth Field
entries.desc: Henry Tudor defeated and killed Richard III, ending the Wars of the Roses and founding the Tudor dynasty.
entries.tldr: Fought on 22 August 1485 in Leicestershire, the battle brought the Wars of the Roses to a decisive end when the Lancastrian claimant Henry Tudor, landing in Wales with a small mercenary force, defeated the Yorkist king Richard III. The battle turned when Lord Stanley and his brother, who had held back while the outcome hung in balance, intervened for Henry, and Richard was killed making a desperate cavalry charge directly at him, the last English king to die in battle. Henry was crowned on the field, founding the Tudor dynasty.

entries.name: Battle of Bannockburn
entries.desc: Robert the Bruce's Scottish forces decisively defeated the English army of Edward II, securing Scottish independence.
entries.tldr: Fought over 23 and 24 June 1314 near Stirling Castle, the battle was the decisive clash of the First War of Scottish Independence, pitting Robert the Bruce's army against a much larger English force under King Edward II sent to relieve the besieged castle. Bruce's disciplined schiltrons of spearmen, aided by ground that hampered English cavalry, broke the advance and drove Edward's army into chaotic retreat. The win did not end the war, which dragged on another fourteen years, but it secured Bruce's throne and remains Scotland's most celebrated military triumph.

entries.name: Chaco War
entries.desc: A brutal war between Bolivia and Paraguay over the arid Gran Chaco region, the deadliest interstate conflict in 20th-century South America.

entries.name: Battle of Rymnik
entries.desc: A decisive Russo-Austrian victory over Ottoman forces during the Russo-Turkish War, led by Alexander Suvorov.

entries.name: Greco-Italian War
entries.desc: Fascist Italy's invasion of Greece, which was repelled by Greek forces and drew Nazi Germany into the Balkan campaign.

entries.name: Battle of Prague
entries.desc: A Prussian victory over Austrian forces early in the Seven Years' War, followed by a costly Prussian siege of the Bohemian capital.

entries.name: Battle of Rovine
entries.desc: Wallachian prince Mircea the Elder repelled an Ottoman invasion force, delaying the Ottoman conquest of Wallachia.

entries.name: Battle of Brunanburh
entries.desc: King Æthelstan's army crushed a coalition of Scots, Vikings, and Strathclyde Britons, a defining moment in English unification.
entries.tldr: Fought in 937 at a still-disputed location in Britain, the battle saw King Æthelstan of England, grandson of Alfred the Great, lead a combined Anglo-Saxon army against an invading coalition of Scots under King Constantine II, Dublin Vikings under Olaf Guthfrithson, and Britons from Strathclyde. Æthelstan's forces crushed the alliance, killing several kings and noblemen among the invaders, in what chroniclers celebrated in verse as an unprecedented slaughter. The victory cemented Æthelstan's claim to be the first true king of a unified England.

entries.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824
entries.desc: Britain and the Netherlands divided their colonial spheres of influence in the Malay Archipelago along the Strait of Malacca.
entries.tldr: Signed in London in March 1824, this treaty resolved decades of overlapping British and Dutch colonial claims in Southeast Asia by dividing the Malay Archipelago along the Strait of Malacca. Britain ceded its settlement at Bencoolen on Sumatra to the Dutch and recognized Dutch dominance south of the strait, while the Netherlands ceded Malacca and dropped claims to the Malay Peninsula and Singapore. The line it drew shaped the later border between British Malaya and the Dutch East Indies, and by extension modern Malaysia and Indonesia.

entries.name: Treaty of Batum
entries.desc: The Ottoman Empire imposed a peace settlement on the newly independent South Caucasus republics of Armenia, Georgia, and Azerbaijan.

entries.name: Anglo-Zulu War
entries.desc: Britain invaded the Zulu Kingdom in southern Africa, suffering a stunning early defeat at Isandlwana before conquering Zululand.
entries.tldr: In January 1879, Britain invaded the independent Zulu Kingdom in southern Africa without authorization from London, seeking to remove it as an obstacle to a planned confederation of colonies. Zulu forces under King Cetshwayo inflicted a stunning defeat on a British column at Isandlwana, killing over a thousand soldiers in one of the worst losses in British colonial warfare. Britain rushed reinforcements and, after fighting including the defense at Rorke's Drift, crushed Zulu resistance at Ulundi in July 1879.

entries.name: Battle of Wadi al-Khaznadar
entries.desc: Mongol Ilkhanate forces under Ghazan Khan defeated the Mamluk Sultanate near Homs, Syria.

entries.name: Battle of the Gates of Trajan
entries.desc: Bulgarian forces under Tsar Samuel ambushed and destroyed a Byzantine army in the mountains of eastern Bulgaria.

entries.name: Treaty of Craiova
entries.desc: Romania ceded Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria under pressure from Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union.

entries.name: Battle of Hunayn
entries.desc: Muhammad's Muslim army defeated the Hawazin and Thaqif tribes near Mecca, securing control of the Arabian Peninsula's holy cities.
entries.tldr: In 630, shortly after the conquest of Mecca, the Hawazin and Thaqif tribes assembled a force to confront the growing Muslim community, ambushing Muhammad's army in the narrow Hunayn valley and initially throwing it into disorder. Muhammad and a core of steadfast companions rallied the fleeing troops, turning the battle into a decisive victory and capturing vast herds of livestock as spoils. The defeat broke Hawazin power, though the town of Ta'if held out under siege before submitting.

entries.name: Battle of Edington
entries.desc: King Alfred the Great of Wessex decisively defeated the Great Heathen Army of Danish Vikings, securing Anglo-Saxon England's survival.
entries.tldr: In May 878, King Alfred the Great of Wessex, having rallied forces from a refuge in the Somerset marshes after a surprise Viking attack, led the West Saxon army to a decisive victory over Guthrum's Great Heathen Army at Edington. The defeated Viking leader agreed to withdraw, accept baptism as Æthelstan, and honor the Treaty of Wedmore, which divided England between Wessex and the Viking-ruled Danelaw. The victory is often seen as the turning point that preserved Anglo-Saxon rule.

entries.name: Morean War
entries.desc: Venice and its Holy League allies fought the Ottoman Empire for control of the Peloponnese peninsula in Greece.

entries.name: Battle of Karánsebes
entries.desc: Austrian army units mistakenly attacked each other in a chaotic nighttime panic during the Austro-Turkish War, inflicting heavy self-caused casualties.

entries.name: Williamite War in Ireland
entries.desc: Supporters of deposed King James II fought forces loyal to William of Orange for control of Ireland and the English throne.

entries.name: Iberian War
entries.desc: The Byzantine and Sasanian Persian empires fought for control of the Caucasian kingdom of Iberia, in modern-day Georgia.

entries.name: Byzantine–Sassanid War of 602–628
entries.desc: The last and most devastating war between the Byzantine and Sasanian Persian empires ended in a decisive Byzantine victory that exhausted both sides before the Arab conquests.

entries.name: Mongol invasion of Central Asia
entries.desc: Genghis Khan's Mongol armies destroyed the Khwarezmian Empire, conquering Transoxiana and Persia's eastern territories.

entries.name: Second Battle of Ypres
entries.desc: German forces used chlorine gas for the first time on the Western Front in an assault on Allied lines near Ypres, Belgium.

entries.name: Second Battle of Bull Run
entries.desc: Confederate forces under Robert E. Lee and Stonewall Jackson decisively defeated the Union Army of Virginia near Manassas, Virginia.

entries.name: Second Battle of St Albans
entries.desc: The Second Battle of St Albans was fought on 17 February 1461 during the Wars of the Roses in St Albans, Hertfordshire, England.

entries.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War
entries.desc: The Second Anglo-Burmese War or the Second Burma War was the second of the three wars fought between the Burmese Empire and British Empire during the 19th century. The war resulted in a British victory with more Burmese territory being annexed to British India.

entries.name: Second Barbary War
entries.desc: The Second Barbary War, also known as the U.S.–Algerian War and the Algerine War, was a brief military conflict between the United States and the North African state of Algiers in 1815.

entries.name: Second Anglo-Afghan War
entries.desc: The Second Anglo-Afghan War was a military conflict fought between the British Raj and the Emirate of Afghanistan from 1878 to 1880, when the latter was ruled by Sher Ali Khan of the Barakzai dynasty, the son of former Emir Dost Mohammad Khan. The war was part of the Great Game between the British and Russian empires.

entries.name: Second Hundred Years' War
entries.desc: The Second Hundred Years' War is a term of periodization, or a historical era designation, coined by J. R. Seeley in his work The Expansion of England (1883).

entries.name: Battle of Hattin
entries.desc: The Battle of Hattin took place on 4 July 1187, between the Crusader states of the Levant and the forces of the Ayyubid sultan Saladin. It is also known as the Battle of the Horns of Hattin, due to the shape of the nearby extinct volcano of that name.
entries.tldr: On 4 July 1187, Saladin's Ayyubid army trapped the exhausted, dehydrated forces of the Kingdom of Jerusalem near a pair of extinct volcanic hills called the Horns of Hattin, after cutting them off from water and burning the dry grass around them. The Crusader army was annihilated, King Guy of Lusignan was captured along with the relic believed to be the True Cross, and most captured Templar and Hospitaller knights were executed. Saladin swiftly overran most of the kingdom's cities, recapturing Jerusalem within three months.

entries.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
entries.desc: Second Anglo-Maratha War was a large conflict within the Maratha Empire involving the East India Company. It resulted in a major loss of territory for the Marathas, including regions around Delhi and in present-day Gujarat falling into direct Company rule.

entries.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
entries.desc: The Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780–1784) saw Mysore's Hyder Ali, backed by France, fight the East India Company across southern India. Neither side gained lasting advantage, and a treaty restored prewar territory.

entries.name: Second Silesian War
entries.desc: The Second Silesian War (1744–1745), part of the wider War of the Austrian Succession, confirmed Prussia's hold on Silesia after Frederick the Great invaded Bohemia. Austria accepted the loss at the Treaty of Dresden.

entries.name: First Battle of the Aisne
entries.desc: The First Battle of the Aisne was the Allied follow-up offensive against the right wing of the German First Army and the Second Army as they retreated after the First Battle of the Marne earlier in September 1914. The Advance to the Aisne consisted of the Battle of the Marne (7–10 September) and the Battle of the Aisne (12–15 September).

entries.name: Battle of Sekigahara
entries.desc: The Battle of Sekigahara was an important battle in Japan which occurred on October 21, 1600 in what is now Gifu Prefecture, Japan, at the end of the Sengoku period.

entries.name: Expulsion of the Moriscos
entries.desc: King Philip III of Spain decreed the expulsion of the Moriscos, Christianized descendants of Spain's Muslim population, in 1609. Roughly 300,000 were deported to North Africa, devastating Spanish agriculture.

entries.name: Battle of Kumanovo
entries.desc: The Battle of Kumanovo, on 23–24 October 1912, was a major battle of the First Balkan War. It was an important Serbian victory over the Ottoman army in the Kosovo Vilayet, shortly after the outbreak of the war. After this defeat, the Ottoman army abandoned the major part of the region, suffering heavy losses in manpower and in war materiel.

entries.name: Battle of the Alamo
entries.desc: The Battle of the Alamo was a pivotal event and military engagement in the Texas Revolution. Following a 13-day siege, Mexican troops under President General Antonio López de Santa Anna reclaimed the Alamo Mission near San Antonio de Béxar.

entries.name: Malayan Emergency
entries.desc: The Malayan Emergency (1948–1960) was a guerrilla war between communist insurgents seeking independence and Commonwealth forces defending colonial Malaya. Counter-insurgency tactics eventually defeated the insurgents.

entries.name: Battle of Buxar
entries.desc: The Battle of Buxar was fought between 22 and 23 October 1764, between the forces of the British East India Company, under the command of Major Hector Munro, against the combined armies of Shah Alam II, the Emperor of the Mughal Empire; Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Bengal; Balwant Singh, the Maharaja of the Benares State; Shuja-ud-daula, the Nawab of Awadh.
entries.tldr: Fought on 22 and 23 October 1764 in the eastern Indian state of Bihar, the battle pitted the British East India Company's forces under Major Hector Munro against a coalition combining Mughal emperor Shah Alam II, deposed Bengal nawab Mir Qasim, and the nawabs of Awadh and Benares. Despite being outnumbered, Munro's better-disciplined force decisively defeated the divided coalition. The win forced the Mughal emperor to grant the Company the diwani, the right to collect revenue over Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, arguably the true foundation of British colonial rule in India.

entries.name: Unification Act
entries.desc: The Unification Act was an agreement signed by the Ukrainian People's Republic and the West Ukrainian People's Republic in Sophia Square in Kyiv on 22 January 1919. Since 1999, it is celebrated every year as the Day of Unity of Ukraine to commemorate the signing of the treaty; it is a state holiday in Ukraine, though not a public holiday.

entries.name: 1948 Ashgabat earthquake
entries.desc: A magnitude-7.3 earthquake struck near Ashgabat, Turkmenistan, on 6 October 1948, devastating the city. Soviet censorship suppressed reporting of the disaster's true scale for decades.
entries.tldr: Shortly after midnight on 6 October 1948, a magnitude-7.3 earthquake struck near Ashgabat, capital of the Turkmen SSR, leveling most of the city's mud-brick buildings within seconds. Casualty estimates range from the tens of thousands to over 100,000, because Soviet authorities classified the true death toll for decades. Survivors described a nighttime catastrophe with little warning, and rebuilding Ashgabat became a major Soviet postwar project. The tragedy's scope only became public after Turkmen independence in 1991.

entries.name: Battle of Arras
entries.desc: A British-led offensive near Arras, France, in 1917 that captured Vimy Ridge and made early gains before stalling into a costly stalemate, at the highest daily casualty rate of any British offensive of the war.
entries.tldr: Launched on 9 April 1917, the British-led offensive near Arras opened with Canadian Corps troops seizing the long-contested high ground of Vimy Ridge in a single coordinated attack. Elsewhere British and Australian forces made rapid early gains using new artillery tactics, but German reserves stiffened and the offensive stalled into the familiar attrition of the Western Front. British forces suffered their highest average daily casualty rate of any offensive in the war, though the battle cemented the Canadian Corps's reputation as an elite formation.

entries.name: Battle of Friedland
entries.desc: On 14 June 1807, Napoleon decisively defeated a Russian army under Levin von Bennigsen at Friedland in East Prussia. The victory forced Russia to negotiate, leading to the Treaties of Tilsit.
entries.tldr: On 14 June 1807, Napoleon lured a Russian army under Levin von Bennigsen into fighting with its back to the Alle River near Friedland in East Prussia, then used a massed artillery bombardment to shatter the Russian formations before infantry finished the rout. Thousands of Russian troops drowned or died trying to retreat across the river's few crossings. The decisive victory ended the War of the Fourth Coalition and forced Tsar Alexander I to negotiate the Treaties of Tilsit, temporarily allying Russia with France.

entries.name: Ukrainian–Soviet War
entries.desc: A war fought between 1917 and 1921 between the Ukrainian People's Republic and the Bolsheviks following the Russian Revolution.

entries.name: Battle of Caporetto
entries.desc: A major World War I battle on the Isonzo front, where German and Austro-Hungarian forces routed the Italian army.
entries.tldr: Beginning on 24 October 1917 along the Isonzo front in the Julian Alps, the battle saw a combined German and Austro-Hungarian force use new infiltration tactics, bypassing strongpoints rather than assaulting them head-on, to shatter Italy's static defensive lines near Caporetto. The surprise assault triggered a catastrophic Italian collapse and retreat of over 100 kilometers to the Piave River, with hundreds of thousands of soldiers killed, wounded, or captured. The disaster forced a change in Italian command, and the name Caporetto entered the language as a byword for total rout.

entries.name: Second Anglo-Sikh war
entries.desc: A war between the Sikh Empire and the East India Company that ended in the fall of the Sikh Empire and annexation of the Punjab.

entries.name: Second Vienna Award
entries.desc: A territorial arbitration by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy that transferred Northern Transylvania from Romania to Hungary.

entries.name: Franco-Russian Alliance
entries.desc: A military alliance between France and Russia formed 1891–94 in response to the Triple Alliance, lasting until 1917.

entries.name: Battle of Liaoyang
entries.desc: A major land battle of the Russo-Japanese War fought near Liaoyang in present-day Liaoning Province, China.

entries.name: Battle of Ain Jalut
entries.desc: A battle between the Mamluks of Egypt and the Mongol Ilkhanate near Ain Jalut, marking the first major halt to Mongol expansion.
entries.tldr: In September 1260, a Mamluk army from Egypt met a Mongol force in the Jezreel Valley near the spring of Ain Jalut, in present-day northern Israel. Using feigned retreats and superior knowledge of the terrain, the Mamluk general Baibars lured the Mongols into an ambush, decisively defeating them and killing their commander Kitbuqa. The victory halted the westward advance of the Mongol Empire, which had already destroyed Baghdad, and preserved Mamluk control of Egypt and the Levant.

entries.name: Siege of Belgrade
entries.desc: The 1456 siege in which Hungarian forces under John Hunyadi repelled an Ottoman attempt to capture Belgrade.

entries.name: Battle of Yamama
entries.desc: A decisive battle of the Ridda Wars in which forces of Caliph Abu Bakr defeated the self-proclaimed prophet Musaylima.

entries.name: Livonian War
entries.desc: A 1558–1583 war for control of Old Livonia between the Tsardom of Russia and a coalition of Nordic and Polish-Lithuanian powers.

entries.name: Battle of Nahrawan
entries.desc: A 658 CE battle in which Caliph Ali's forces defeated the Kharijites, former allies who had broken with him after Siffin.

entries.name: Muslim conquest of the Levant
entries.desc: The Rashidun Caliphate's conquest of Byzantine Syria between 634–638 CE, part of the wider early Muslim conquests.

entries.name: War of the Third Coalition
entries.desc: The first conflict of the Napoleonic Wars, pitting Napoleon's France against a coalition led by Britain, Austria, and Russia.

entries.name: Battle of Tarawa
entries.desc: A bloody 1943 amphibious battle between the US and Japan on Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands, part of Operation Galvanic.

entries.name: Battle of Sarikamish
entries.desc: A disastrous World War I engagement between Russian and Ottoman forces in the Caucasus campaign, fought in winter 1914–15.

entries.name: Hungarian–Romanian War
entries.desc: A 1918–1919 war between Hungary and Romania fought amid the collapse of Austria-Hungary after World War I.

entries.name: Italian War of 1551–1559
entries.desc: A war begun by Henry II of France against Charles V for control of Italy, ended by the Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis.

entries.name: Crimean War
entries.desc: A war fought 1853–56 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, France, Britain, and Sardinia over the Eastern Question.

entries.name: Battle of Shanghai
entries.desc: A major 1937 battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War fought in Shanghai, among the largest battles of the entire war.

entries.name: Great stand on the Ugra river
entries.desc: An 1480 standoff on the Ugra River between Akhmat Khan of the Great Horde and Grand Prince Ivan III of Moscow, ending Mongol rule over Russia.

entries.name: Battle of Baku
entries.desc: A 1918 battle for control of Baku fought between Ottoman-Azerbaijani forces and Bolshevik-Armenian Baku Commune defenders, later reinforced by British troops.
entries.tldr: Fought in the summer and autumn of 1918 amid the Russian Empire's collapse, the battle for oil-rich Baku pitted an Ottoman-led force allied with the new Azerbaijan Democratic Republic against the Bolshevik and Dashnak-led Baku Commune, briefly reinforced by a small British detachment under General Lionel Dunsterville. After the British withdrew in the face of superior numbers, Ottoman and Azerbaijani troops stormed the city on 15 September 1918, and its fall was accompanied by mass killings of Baku's Armenian population. Control of the oil fields was the central strategic prize.

entries.name: Anastasian War
entries.desc: A war fought from 502 to 506 between the Byzantine and Sasanian empires, the first major conflict between the two powers in over sixty years.
entries.tldr: Fought from 502 to 506 between the Eastern Roman emperor Anastasius I and the Sasanian shah Kavad I, this war was the first major clash between Rome and Persia in over six decades. Kavad, needing funds after Rome refused to help pay tribute to the Huns, opened the war by storming the fortress city of Amida. Fighting see-sawed across Mesopotamia until both sides, distracted by other frontiers, agreed to a truce. Anastasius then built the fortress city of Dara to guard the frontier.

entries.name: Wars of the Three Kingdoms
entries.desc: A series of conflicts from 1639 to 1653 across England, Scotland and Ireland, including the English Civil Wars and the Irish Confederate Wars.

entries.name: First Egyptian-Ottoman War
entries.desc: An 1831–1833 conflict in which Egyptian forces under Muhammad Ali Pasha seized Ottoman Syria, demanding it as reward for aiding the sultan in the Greek War of Independence.

entries.name: War of Devolution
entries.desc: A 1667–1668 war in which France occupied the Spanish Netherlands and Franche-Comté, with Louis XIV claiming the territories through his wife's inheritance rights.

entries.name: Treaty of Gandamak
entries.desc: An 1879 treaty ending the first phase of the Second Anglo-Afghan War, in which Afghan emir Mohammad Yaqub Khan ceded frontier territory and control of foreign affairs to Britain.

entries.name: Second Egyptian-Ottoman War
entries.desc: An 1839–1841 conflict, also called the Second Syrian War, fought mainly in Syria between Egyptian and Ottoman forces.

entries.name: War of 1812
entries.desc: A conflict from 1812 to 1815 between the United States and Britain, fought mainly in North America and at sea amid the wider Napoleonic Wars.

entries.name: Capture of Rome
entries.desc: The 1870 seizure of Rome and the Papal States by forces of the Kingdom of Italy, completing the unification of Italy.

entries.name: Battles of Rzhev
entries.desc: A series of costly Red Army offensives against the Wehrmacht around Rzhev from January 1942 to March 1943 on the Eastern Front of World War II.

entries.name: Battle of Konotop
entries.desc: A 1659 battle in which a Cossack coalition under Hetman Ivan Vyhovsky defeated Russian Tsardom cavalry near Konotop, Ukraine, during the Russo-Polish War.

entries.name: Japanese coup d'état in French Indochina
entries.desc: A March 1945 Japanese operation that overthrew French colonial rule in Indochina as Japan faced imminent Allied invasion late in World War II.

entries.name: Battle of Tolbiac
entries.desc: A battle between the Franks under Clovis I and the Alamanni, traditionally dated to 496, near what is now Zülpich, Germany.

entries.name: German invasion of the Netherlands
entries.desc: A May 1940 German military campaign that overran the Netherlands in days, part of the wider invasion of the Low Countries and France.

entries.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
entries.desc: An 1040 battle in which the Seljuq Turks decisively defeated the Ghaznavid Empire near Merv, ending Ghaznavid dominance over Greater Khorasan.
entries.tldr: In 1040, Seljuk Turk forces led by brothers Tughril and Chaghri Beg decisively defeated the army of the Ghaznavid sultan Mas'ud I near Merv in Greater Khorasan. Mas'ud, who had underestimated the Seljuks after years of raiding, fled the field and was later killed in a subsequent coup. The victory ended Ghaznavid dominance over Khorasan and Persia and is traditionally seen as the founding moment of the Seljuk Empire, which Tughril proclaimed sultan soon after.

entries.name: Northwest Indian War
entries.desc: A conflict for control of the Northwest Territory between the United States and a confederation of Native American nations, considered the first American Indian War.

entries.name: Prussian Crusade
entries.desc: A 13th-century series of campaigns by the Teutonic Knights and other Catholic crusaders to conquer and Christianize the pagan Old Prussians.

entries.name: War of the Second Coalition
entries.desc: An 1798–1802 war between revolutionary France and a coalition of European monarchies led by Britain, Austria and Russia.

entries.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1716–1718
entries.desc: The Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718) was fought between the Habsburg monarchy and the Ottoman Empire. The 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz was not an acceptable permanent agreement for the Ottoman Empire.
entries.tldr: Seeking to reverse losses from the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz, the Ottoman Empire went to war against Venice in 1714, prompting the Habsburg monarchy to intervene on Venice's behalf in 1716. Austrian forces led by the celebrated general Prince Eugene of Savoy won major victories at Petrovaradin and, after a lengthy siege, captured the fortress city of Belgrade in 1717. The 1718 Treaty of Passarowitz ended the war, with the Ottomans ceding Belgrade, northern Serbia, and parts of Wallachia to Austria.

entries.name: Dieppe Raid
entries.desc: Operation Jubilee or the Dieppe Raid was an Allied amphibious attack on the German-occupied port of Dieppe in northern France, during the Second World War.

entries.name: Vlora War
entries.desc: The Vlora War or Vlora crisis was a military conflict in the Vlorë region of Albania between the Kingdom of Italy and Albanian nationalists.

entries.name: Second Battle of Homs
entries.desc: The Second Battle of Homs was fought in western Syria on 29 October 1281, between the armies of the Mamluk dynasty of Egypt and the Ilkhanate, a division of the Mongol Empire centered on Iran.

entries.name: Battle of Marengo
entries.desc: The Battle of Marengo was fought on 14 June 1800 between French forces under the First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte and Austrian forces near the city of Alessandria, in Piedmont, Italy.

entries.name: Battle of Lechfeld
entries.desc: The Battle of Lechfeld was a series of military engagements over three days in August 955 in which the Kingdom of Germany, led by Otto I, defeated the Hungarian army.

entries.name: Battle of Karnal
entries.desc: The Battle of Karnal was a decisive victory for Nader Shah, founder of the Afsharid dynasty of Iran, during his invasion of India, defeating the army of Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah.

entries.name: Lithuanian Wars of Independence
entries.desc: The Lithuanian Wars of Independence, also known as the Freedom Struggles, refer to three wars Lithuania fought defending its independence at the end of World War I.

entries.name: Battle of Vitoria
entries.desc: At the Battle of Vitoria, a British, Portuguese and Spanish army under the Marquess of Wellington broke the French army near Vitoria in Spain, a decisive Peninsular War victory.

entries.name: Aceh War
entries.desc: The Aceh War was an armed military conflict between the Sultanate of Aceh and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, part of the Dutch conquest of Sumatra and Indonesia.
entries.tldr: Beginning in 1873, the Netherlands invaded the independent Sultanate of Aceh in northern Sumatra to complete its control over the Indonesian archipelago. Dutch forces captured the sultan's palace early on but faced decades of tenacious guerrilla resistance led by religious and local leaders across Aceh's difficult terrain. The conflict dragged on with immense casualties until Dutch "pacification" campaigns finally suppressed organized resistance in the early twentieth century. It stands as one of the longest, costliest wars of Dutch colonial expansion.

entries.name: Battle of Crécy
entries.desc: The Battle of Crécy took place on 26 August 1346 in northern France between a French army under King Philip VI and an English army under King Edward III, an English victory in the Hundred Years' War.
entries.tldr: Fought on 26 August 1346 near Crécy in northern France, this was the first major land battle of the Hundred Years' War and a turning point in medieval warfare. King Edward III positioned English and Welsh longbowmen on a hillside, where their volleys shredded the advancing Genoese crossbowmen and repeated French cavalry charges. Edward's teenage son, later the Black Prince, held the vanguard and won his spurs in the fighting. The lopsided defeat shattered French confidence and paved the way for Edward's capture of Calais the next year.

entries.name: Siege of Constantinople
entries.desc: Constantinople, built on the land linking Europe to Asia, had strategic value for many empires and kingdoms who tried to conquer it throughout history.

entries.name: First Battle of Gaza
entries.desc: The First Battle of Gaza was fought on 26 March 1917 during the first attempt by the Egyptian Expeditionary Force to advance through Gaza in the Sinai and Palestine Campaign of the First World War.

entries.name: Battle of Benevento
entries.desc: The Battle of Benevento was fought on 26 February 1266 near Benevento in southern Italy between the forces of Charles I of Anjou and King Manfred of Sicily, ending Hohenstaufen rule in Italy.
entries.tldr: Fought on 26 February 1266 near Benevento in southern Italy, the battle pitted Charles of Anjou, brother of the French king and papal candidate for the Sicilian crown, against King Manfred, illegitimate son of Emperor Frederick II, who had inherited Sicily's throne. Manfred's army, weakened by the defection of unreliable Italian allies, was defeated, and Manfred was killed in the fighting, his body reportedly denied Christian burial as an excommunicate. The victory installed Charles as king of Sicily and permanently ended Hohenstaufen rule over southern Italy.

entries.name: Battle of Legnano
entries.desc: The Battle of Legnano was fought between the imperial army of Frederick Barbarossa and the troops of the Lombard League on 29 May 1176, near Legnano in present-day Lombardy, Italy.

entries.name: Ninth Russo-Turkish War
entries.desc: The Russo-Turkish War of 1828–1829 resulted from the Greek War of Independence; war broke out after the Ottoman Sultan closed the Dardanelles to Russian ships.

entries.name: Cisplatine War
entries.desc: The Cisplatine War was an armed conflict fought in the 1820s between the Empire of Brazil and the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata over control of the Banda Oriental.

entries.name: Battle of the Zab
entries.desc: The Battle of the Zab took place on 25 January 750, on the banks of the Great Zab in what is now Iraq, spelling the end of the Umayyad Caliphate and the rise of the Abbasid Caliphate.

entries.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
entries.desc: The first of three wars between the British East India Company and the Konbaung dynasty of Burma, ending in a costly but decisive British victory.

entries.name: Battle of Singapore
entries.desc: Japanese forces captured Singapore from the British in February 1942, one of the largest surrenders in British military history.

entries.name: Battle of Salsu
entries.desc: Goguryeo forces annihilated a vastly larger Sui Chinese army at the Salsu River, a decisive victory in the Goguryeo–Sui War.

entries.name: Battle of Asiago
entries.desc: Austro-Hungarian forces launched a major offensive on the Asiago plateau against Italy during World War I's Italian Front.
entries.tldr: Also called the Strafexpedition, or punitive expedition, by the Austro-Hungarian command, the offensive launched in May 1916 aimed to break the Italian front on the Asiago plateau and punish Italy for switching sides against its former ally in 1915. Austro-Hungarian troops made strong early gains against surprised defenders, advancing several kilometers, but supply trouble in the mountains and Russian pressure elsewhere stalled the attack. Italian counterattacks through June recovered much of the ground, leaving a costly, inconclusive campaign for Vienna.

entries.name: Franco-Syrian War
entries.desc: French forces defeated King Faisal's Arab Kingdom of Syria and entered Damascus, establishing the French Mandate over Syria.

entries.name: Battle of Brandywine
entries.desc: British forces under General Howe defeated Washington's Continental Army near Chadds Ford, Pennsylvania, during the American Revolutionary War.
entries.tldr: Fought on 11 September 1777 near Chadds Ford, Pennsylvania, the battle was the largest single-day engagement of the Revolutionary War, as British forces under General William Howe outmaneuvered George Washington's Continental Army by crossing the Brandywine Creek upstream and hitting its exposed flank. Despite resistance from units including the wounded Marquis de Lafayette, Washington's army was forced into a disorganized retreat, opening the road to Philadelphia, occupied by the British two weeks later. The army's survival let it fight on and eventually winter at Valley Forge.

entries.name: Battle of Adwa
entries.desc: Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II decisively defeated an invading Italian army, securing Ethiopian independence.
entries.tldr: On 1 March 1896, a large Ethiopian army led by Emperor Menelik II overwhelmed an invading Italian colonial force near the town of Adwa in northern Ethiopia. Poor Italian intelligence and overconfidence led three separated columns into disaster against Menelik's larger, well-armed force, with thousands of Italian and colonial troops killed or captured. The defeat forced Italy to recognize Ethiopian sovereignty, making Ethiopia the only African state to repel a European colonial conquest during the Scramble for Africa.

entries.name: Alaska Purchase
entries.desc: The United States purchased Alaska from the Russian Empire for $7.2 million, extending American territory into the Arctic.
entries.tldr: In 1867, US Secretary of State William Seward negotiated the purchase of Alaska from the Russian Empire for $7.2 million, roughly two cents per acre. Russia sold the territory partly for fear of losing it without compensation in a future war, particularly to Britain, and because the fur trade that justified the colony was in decline. American critics mocked the deal as "Seward's Folly," doubting the value of the remote territory. The later discovery of gold and oil proved it enormously valuable.

entries.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
entries.desc: British forces defeated the French outside Quebec City in a turning point of the Seven Years' War that led to British control of Canada.

entries.name: Battle of Nördlingen
entries.desc: Catholic Habsburg forces crushed the Protestant Swedish army at Nördlingen, a major turning point of the Thirty Years' War.

entries.name: Battle of Leuthen
entries.desc: Frederick the Great's Prussian army used maneuver and terrain to rout a much larger Austrian force, securing control of Silesia.

entries.name: Battle of the Dnieper
entries.desc: One of the largest operations of World War II, Soviet forces crossed the Dnieper River and drove German forces from Ukraine's eastern bank.

entries.name: First English Civil War
entries.desc: War between Royalists and Parliamentarians in England and Wales, part of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms, that reshaped English governance.

entries.name: Burgundian Wars
entries.desc: Conflict between the Duchy of Burgundy and the Swiss Confederacy in which Charles the Bold was defeated repeatedly and killed at Nancy.

entries.name: Thirteen Years' War
entries.desc: War between the Prussian Confederation, backed by Poland, and the Teutonic Order, ending Teutonic dominance over western Prussia.

entries.name: Battle of Oudenarde
entries.desc: Anglo-Dutch forces under Marlborough and Prince Eugene defeated the French army during the War of the Spanish Succession.

entries.name: Battle of Nancy
entries.desc: René II of Lorraine and the Swiss Confederacy defeated and killed Charles the Bold, ending Burgundian power in Lorraine.

entries.name: Battle of Malplaquet
entries.desc: One of the bloodiest battles of the 18th century; the Grand Alliance under Marlborough won a costly victory over the French in the War of the Spanish Succession.

entries.name: Hindenburg disaster
entries.desc: The German airship Hindenburg caught fire and was destroyed while attempting to dock in New Jersey, killing 36 people and ending the airship era.

entries.name: Mahdist War
entries.desc: Muhammad Ahmad's Mahdist Sudanese forces overthrew Ottoman-Egyptian rule and later fought the British, establishing an independent Mahdist state in Sudan.

entries.name: Battle of Almansa
entries.desc: Decisive Bourbon victory over Habsburg forces during the War of the Spanish Succession, securing Philip V's hold on Spain.
entries.tldr: Fought on 25 April 1707 during the War of the Spanish Succession, the battle saw a Bourbon army under the exiled English general the Duke of Berwick crush a smaller Habsburg force under the Earl of Galway near Almansa in southeastern Spain. Poor coordination among the Allies' Portuguese, English, and Dutch contingents let their cavalry collapse. The defeat effectively ended Habsburg hopes of putting Archduke Charles on the Spanish throne, letting Philip V overrun Valencia and Aragon and abolish their historic local liberties, centralizing Spain under Bourbon rule.

entries.name: Battle of Solferino
entries.desc: Franco-Piedmontese victory over Austria that was the climactic battle of the Second Italian War of Independence.

entries.name: Siege of Acre
entries.desc: Mamluk capture of the last Crusader stronghold in the Holy Land, ending nearly two centuries of Crusader presence in the Levant.

entries.name: Battle of Marston Moor
entries.desc: Parliamentarian and Scottish Covenanter victory over Royalist forces, the largest battle of the Wars of the Three Kingdoms.

entries.name: Nakba
entries.desc: Mass displacement and dispossession of Palestinian Arabs accompanying the establishment of Israel in 1948.

entries.name: Battle of Morgarten
entries.desc: Swiss Confederate ambush that destroyed an invading Austrian army, a founding victory of the Old Swiss Confederacy.

entries.name: Battle of Gazala
entries.desc: Axis victory over British Commonwealth forces in the Western Desert Campaign that led to the fall of Tobruk.
entries.tldr: Fought from late May to mid-June 1942 in the Libyan desert west of Tobruk, this battle saw Field Marshal Erwin Rommel's Axis forces outmaneuver a numerically superior British Eighth Army despite becoming briefly trapped in a defensive pocket nicknamed 'the Cauldron.' Rommel resupplied his encircled units through a gap in British minefields and broke out to shatter the Allied defensive 'boxes' one by one, forcing a British retreat. The victory led directly to the fall of Tobruk days later.

entries.name: Operation Nordwind
entries.desc: Last major German offensive on the Western Front, launched to relieve pressure from the Battle of the Bulge.

entries.name: Battle of Aachen
entries.desc: Bitter urban battle in which American forces captured the first major German city of World War II.
entries.tldr: In October 1944, American forces of the US First Army fought their way into Aachen, the first major German city to fall to the Allies in the Second World War and symbolically significant as Charlemagne's historic seat. Hitler ordered the city defended to the last man, leading to nearly three weeks of brutal house-to-house urban combat. American troops eventually reduced German strongpoints with tanks and artillery firing point-blank through city streets, forcing a garrison surrender on 21 October.

entries.name: Battle of Białystok–Minsk
entries.desc: German encirclement that destroyed two Soviet armies in the opening days of Operation Barbarossa.
entries.tldr: Fought over the last week of June 1941, the battle came in the opening days of Operation Barbarossa, Nazi Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union, as Army Group Centre's panzer pincers raced ahead of the infantry to encircle Soviet forces around Białystok and Minsk. Two entire Soviet armies, plus parts of several others, were trapped in the resulting pockets and largely destroyed, with several hundred thousand soldiers killed, captured, or missing. The encirclement exposed the Red Army's disorganization after Stalin's prewar purges and opened the road toward Smolensk and Moscow.

entries.name: Battle of Uman
entries.desc: German offensive that encircled and annihilated two Soviet armies near Uman, Ukraine, in 1941.

entries.name: Machtergreifung
entries.desc: Adolf Hitler's rise to the German chancellorship and the Nazi Party's subsequent consolidation of dictatorial power.

entries.name: Battle of Varna
entries.desc: Ottoman victory over a Crusader army led by Władysław III of Poland and Hungary, ending the Crusade of Varna.

entries.name: First Boer War
entries.desc: Boer victory over British forces in the Transvaal that restored South African Republic independence.

entries.name: War of the Austrian Succession
entries.desc: Multi-power European conflict sparked by Maria Theresa's succession to the Habsburg throne.

entries.name: Battle of Marignano
entries.desc: French and Venetian victory over the Old Swiss Confederacy that ended the War of the League of Cambrai.

entries.name: Battle of Gettysburg
entries.desc: Union victory over Confederate forces widely regarded as the turning point of the American Civil War.
entries.tldr: Fought over three days, 1–3 July 1863, near the Pennsylvania town of Gettysburg, this was the largest and bloodiest battle ever fought in North America, with roughly 50,000 combined casualties. Confederate General Robert E. Lee's second invasion of the North culminated on the final day in Pickett's Charge, a doomed frontal assault on entrenched Union positions repulsed with devastating losses. The Union victory marked the strategic high-water mark of the Confederacy, which never again invaded the North.

entries.name: Battle of Eylau
entries.desc: Bloody, inconclusive clash between Napoleon's Grande Armée and Russian forces in East Prussia.
entries.tldr: Fought in a blinding snowstorm on 7–8 February 1807 near the East Prussian town of Eylau, this battle pitted Napoleon's Grande Armée against a Russian army under Levin von Bennigsen, reinforced by Prussian troops. When Russian artillery shattered a French corps, Marshal Joachim Murat led one of history's largest cavalry charges to stabilize the French line. Both sides suffered appalling casualties, and neither achieved a clear victory. The battle's cost shocked French opinion and foreshadowed the bloodier stalemates of later campaigns.

entries.name: Seven Years' War
entries.desc: Global conflict pitting Britain and Prussia against France, Austria, and their allies across Europe, the Americas, and India.

entries.name: Battle of the Pyramids
entries.desc: Napoleon's victory over Ottoman Egyptian forces near Cairo during the French invasion of Egypt.

entries.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
entries.desc: On 17 June 1775, British troops took the Charlestown peninsula near Boston from American militia in a costly frontal assault. Britain's heavy casualties in the technical victory showed the war would not be quickly won.
entries.tldr: Fought on 17 June 1775 during the early siege of Boston, the battle takes its name from Bunker Hill though most fighting occurred on adjacent Breed's Hill, where colonial militia had hastily fortified a position overlooking the city. British troops under General William Howe launched repeated frontal assaults up the hill against entrenched Americans, who inflicted devastating casualties before running low on ammunition and withdrawing. Though a technical British victory, the huge cost stunned London and showed the rebellion would not be swiftly crushed.

entries.name: Battle of Monte Cassino
entries.desc: Fought across four Allied assaults between January and May 1944, this battle broke the German Gustav Line defenses south of Rome, at the cost of the historic abbey's destruction, and opened the road to Rome.

entries.name: Battle of Grunwald
entries.desc: On 15 July 1410, a Polish–Lithuanian–Ruthenian army decisively defeated the Teutonic Knights near Grunwald, killing the order's Grand Master. The defeat broke the Teutonic Order's military dominance in the region.
entries.tldr: On 15 July 1410, a Polish–Lithuanian–Ruthenian army led by King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas annihilated the Teutonic Knights near the villages of Grunwald and Tannenberg, killing Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen along with most of the order's senior leadership. It ranks among the largest battles of medieval Europe and one of the most decisive defeats the order ever suffered. Although the order survived a siege of its capital at Marienburg, the battle permanently broke its military dominance.

entries.name: Battle of Großbeeren
entries.desc: On 23 August 1813, Prussian forces under Friedrich von Bülow defeated a Franco-Saxon corps south of Berlin. The victory blocked a French advance on the city during the War of the Sixth Coalition.
entries.tldr: On 23 August 1813, Prussian troops under General Friedrich von Bülow intercepted a Franco-Saxon corps under Marshal Nicolas Oudinot as it advanced on Berlin as part of Napoleon's plan to seize the Prussian capital. Despite rain-soaked terrain, Bülow's forces broke the advancing columns and forced Oudinot into a disorganized retreat, abandoning the offensive. The victory, largely won by Prussian Landwehr militia, preserved Berlin during the War of the Sixth Coalition.

entries.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
entries.desc: The Battle of the Milvian Bridge took place between the Roman Emperors Constantine I and Maxentius on 28 October AD 312. It takes its name from the Milvian Bridge, an important route over the Tiber.

entries.name: transition from Ming to Qing
entries.desc: The transition from Ming to Qing was a decades-long conquest of China by the Manchu-led Qing dynasty, beginning with Nurhaci's unification of the Jurchen tribes in 1616. It ended Ming rule over China.

entries.name: Battle of Okehazama
entries.desc: On 12 June 1560, Oda Nobunaga's greatly outnumbered forces ambushed and killed rival warlord Imagawa Yoshimoto, an upset victory that launched Nobunaga's rise toward unifying Japan.

entries.name: Adams–Onís Treaty
entries.desc: Signed in 1819 by John Quincy Adams and Luis de Onís, this treaty ceded Spanish Florida to the United States and fixed the western border between the US and New Spain along a line to the Pacific.
entries.tldr: Negotiated by US Secretary of State John Quincy Adams and Spanish minister Luis de Onís, this treaty, signed in 1819 and ratified in 1821, ceded all of Spanish Florida to the United States in exchange for the US assuming $5 million in claims by American citizens against Spain. It also drew a definitive boundary between Louisiana Territory and Spain's remaining possessions, running to the Pacific and confirming US claims to Oregon. It followed years of tension over Florida, including Andrew Jackson's unauthorized incursions there.

entries.name: Partitio terrarum imperii Romaniae
entries.desc: The Partitio terrarum imperii Romaniae was the 1204 treaty dividing the conquered Byzantine Empire among the crusaders after they sacked Constantinople. It created a patchwork of Latin states on former Byzantine soil.

entries.name: Arab conquest of Armenia
entries.desc: A series of Rashidun Caliphate campaigns from 639 to 661 against Byzantine-held Armenia. The fighting brought Armenia under Arab suzerainty while its local nakharar princes retained considerable autonomy.
entries.tldr: Between 639 and 661, armies of the Rashidun Caliphate launched repeated campaigns into Armenia, then contested between Byzantine and Sasanian influence, eventually bringing the region under Arab suzerainty. Rather than direct rule, the caliphate let Armenia's local nakharar noble families keep considerable autonomy over their hereditary territories in exchange for tribute and nominal submission. This let Armenian Christian culture and church institutions survive largely intact under Muslim overlordship for centuries.

entries.name: Battle of Khotyn
entries.desc:
Battle of Khotyn can refer to several battles that took place near Khotyn:Battle of Khotyn (1509)
Battle of Khotyn (1530)
Battle of Khotyn (1621)
Battle of Khotyn (1673)
Siege of Khotyn (1788)

entries.name: Anglo-Spanish War
entries.desc: A conflict from 1654 to 1660 in which Oliver Cromwell's England attacked Spain's American and European possessions as part of the "Western Design." England seized Jamaica from Spain during the fighting.
entries.tldr: Launched in 1654 as part of Oliver Cromwell's "Western Design" to weaken Catholic Spain's American empire, this war saw an English fleet fail to capture Santo Domingo but succeed in seizing the lightly defended island of Jamaica in 1655. Fighting spread to European waters, where English admirals like Robert Blake intercepted Spanish treasure convoys and won a notable victory at Santa Cruz de Tenerife. Spain, weakened by its parallel war with France, could not recapture Jamaica. The war ended in 1660 with English possession of Jamaica confirmed.

entries.name: Siege of Baghdad
entries.desc: The 1258 Siege of Baghdad saw a Mongol army under Hulegu Khan capture and sack the city, killing the last Abbasid caliph and ending the Abbasid Caliphate's five centuries of rule.

entries.name: Battle of Tippecanoe
entries.desc: On 7 November 1811, American forces under William Henry Harrison defeated Tecumseh's Native confederacy while Tecumseh was away, dispersing the alliance and giving Harrison a reputation he later rode to the presidency.

entries.name: Caucasian War
entries.desc: A prolonged conflict in which the Russian Empire subdued the peoples of the North Caucasus who resisted subjugation during the Russian conquest of the region, ending in annexation and the mass expulsion of Circassians.

entries.name: Siege of Damascus
entries.desc: The 1148 Siege of Damascus was the main campaign of the Second Crusade: crusader forces besieged the Muslim-ruled city before abandoning the effort after only four days, effectively ending the crusade.

entries.name: Battle of Saragarhi
entries.desc: On 12 September 1897, 21 soldiers of the 36th Sikhs held a signalling post against thousands of Afghan tribesmen, fighting to the last man; the stand is remembered as one of history's celebrated last stands.

entries.name: Battle of Kohima
entries.desc: Fought from April to June 1944, this battle halted Japan's invasion of British India; combined with the victory at Imphal, it forced a costly Japanese retreat and marked the turning point of the Burma campaign.

entries.name: Battle of Mukden
entries.desc: Fought from February to March 1905, this was the largest land battle fought before World War I; Japan's victory over the Russian army effectively ended Russian land resistance in the Russo-Japanese War.

entries.name: Battle of the Yalu River
entries.desc: On 17 September 1894, Japan's navy decisively defeated China's Beiyang Fleet at the mouth of the Yalu River, establishing Japanese naval supremacy for the remainder of the First Sino-Japanese War.

entries.name: Battle of Dara
entries.desc: The Battle of Dara was fought between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanians in 530 AD. It was one of the battles of the Iberian War.
entries.tldr: Fought in 530 near the fortress city of Dara on the Byzantine-Persian frontier, this battle pitted a Sasanian army under the general Perozes against a smaller East Roman force commanded by the young general Belisarius. Using field fortifications and disciplined cavalry reserves, Belisarius routed the larger Persian force. It was Belisarius's first major victory and established his reputation as Emperor Justinian I's leading general, during the Iberian War over control of the Caucasus.

entries.name: Ōnin War
entries.desc: The Ōnin War (1467–1477) was a civil war among rival samurai clans over succession disputes during Japan's Muromachi period. Its devastation of Kyoto and the shogunate's weakened authority ushered in the Sengoku era.

entries.name: Treaty of Hadiach
entries.desc: The Treaty of Hadiach was a treaty signed on 16 September 1658 in Hadiach, Cossack Hetmanate between representatives of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and Zaporozhian Cossacks.

entries.name: Battle of Arnhem
entries.desc: The Battle of Arnhem was fought during the Second World War, as part of the Allied Operation Market Garden. It took place around the Dutch city of Arnhem from 17 to 26 September 1944.
entries.tldr: Fought from 17 to 26 September 1944, the battle was the disastrous climax of Operation Market Garden, an Allied plan to seize a chain of bridges across the Netherlands and outflank German defenses. British and Polish airborne troops landed near Arnhem to capture the Rhine road bridge, but ground forces advancing overland were delayed, and the paratroopers met unexpectedly strong German armor. A small force under Lieutenant Colonel John Frost held the bridge four days before being overwhelmed, and the failed effort ended Allied hopes of finishing the war in 1944.

entries.name: Battle of Stalingrad
entries.desc: Fought from August 1942 to February 1943, Soviet forces encircled and destroyed Germany's Sixth Army in the deadliest battle in history, marking the turning point of World War II on the Eastern Front.

entries.name: Battle of Yamazaki
entries.desc: The Battle of Yamazaki  was fought in 1582 in Yamazaki, Japan, located in current-day Kyoto Prefecture. This battle is sometimes referred to as the Battle of Mt.

entries.name: Battle of Soissons
entries.desc: In 486, Frankish king Clovis I defeated the Roman general Syagrius near Soissons, ending the last vestige of Roman rule in northern Gaul and opening the region to Frankish control.

entries.name: Siege of Orléans
entries.desc: The Siege of Orléans (1428–1429) was the turning point of the Hundred Years' War: English forces besieged the city until Joan of Arc rallied French troops to break the siege, reviving French morale.

entries.name: Battle of Sagrajas
entries.desc: In 1086, Almoravid forces under Yusuf ibn Tashfin defeated Alfonso VI of Castile at Sagrajas, checking the Christian reconquest of Iberia and opening al-Andalus to decades of Almoravid rule.

entries.name: Battle of Vimy Ridge
entries.desc: In April 1917, the four divisions of the Canadian Corps captured German-held Vimy Ridge in a costly, coordinated assault that is remembered in Canada as a defining moment of national identity.

entries.name: Treaty of Paris
entries.desc: Treaty of Paris may refer to one of many treaties signed in Paris, France:

entries.name: Third Geneva Convention
entries.desc: The Third Geneva Convention of 1949 set standards for the humane treatment of prisoners of war. It expanded protections established after the mistreatment of POWs during the Second World War.

entries.name: Battle of Coronel
entries.desc: On 1 November 1914, a German East Asia Squadron under Maximilian von Spee defeated a British squadron under Christopher Cradock off Chile, sinking two cruisers. It was the Royal Navy's first defeat at sea in a century.
entries.tldr: On 1 November 1914 off central Chile, Vice Admiral Maximilian von Spee's German East Asia Squadron intercepted a weaker British force under Sir Christopher Cradock. German gunnery sank the armored cruisers HMS Good Hope and HMS Monmouth with the loss of all hands, including Cradock, while the German ships suffered barely a scratch. It was the Royal Navy's first defeat at sea in over a century. London responded by dispatching battlecruisers that annihilated von Spee's squadron five weeks later at the Falkland Islands.

entries.name: Battle of Dettingen
entries.desc: Fought on 27 June 1743 near Dettingen in Bavaria during the War of the Austrian Succession, an allied army defeated the French. It was the last time a reigning British monarch personally led troops into battle.
entries.tldr: On 27 June 1743, the 'Pragmatic Army' of British, Hanoverian, and Austrian troops, personally led by King George II, defeated a French force under the Duc de Noailles near Dettingen in Bavaria during the War of the Austrian Succession. The French had nearly trapped the allies against the Main River, but a premature cavalry charge let the allied infantry escape and drive the French back. George II fought on foot after his horse bolted, the last reigning British monarch to lead troops personally in battle.

entries.name: Battle of Pliska
entries.desc: In July 811, Bulgarian forces under Khan Krum ambushed and destroyed the Byzantine army in the Balkan passes, killing Emperor Nicephorus I, whose skull Krum reportedly had made into a drinking cup.

entries.name: Attack of the Dead Men
entries.desc: The Attack of the Dead Men, or the Battle of Osowiec Fortress, was a battle of World War I that took place at Osowiec Fortress, at 4:00 AM on August 6, 1915.
entries.tldr: During the German siege of the Russian-held Osowiec Fortress in present-day Poland, German forces released chlorine gas before attacking at 4 a.m. on 6 August 1915, expecting the garrison wiped out. Instead, surviving Russian defenders of the 226th Zemlyansky Regiment, badly burned and coughing blood from the gas, mounted a desperate bayonet counterattack. The horrifying sight of these disfigured, dying soldiers reportedly panicked the German attackers into a chaotic retreat, a legend of Russian wartime endurance.

entries.name: Battle of Denain
entries.desc: On 24 July 1712, French forces under Marshal Villars defeated a Dutch and Austrian army near Denain during the War of the Spanish Succession, reversing France's decline and easing peace terms at Utrecht.
entries.tldr: On 24 July 1712, Marshal Claude de Villars led a surprise French assault across the Scheldt to storm the fortified camp at Denain, overwhelming the Dutch garrison before Prince Eugene of Savoy's main allied army could intervene. The victory, achieved when France's fortunes in the War of the Spanish Succession looked hopeless, let Villars roll up allied supply depots and fortresses along the frontier. It restored French bargaining power and eased the terms France secured in the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht.

entries.name: Second Opium War
entries.desc: The Second Opium War (1856–1860) was fought by Britain and France against Qing China to expand trading rights, including the legalization of opium. China's defeat forced further concessions, including more treaty ports.

entries.name: Battle of New Orleans
entries.desc: On 8 January 1815, Andrew Jackson's American forces decisively defeated the British army outside New Orleans, fought after the war-ending Treaty of Ghent had already been signed, and made Jackson a national hero.

entries.name: Philippine Revolution
entries.desc: The Philippine Revolution (1896–1898) was an independence war waged by the Katipunan movement against Spanish colonial rule. It ended over 300 years of Spanish rule but was soon followed by American annexation.

entries.name: Gunboat War
entries.desc: Naval conflict between Denmark–Norway and Britain, supported by Sweden, during the Napoleonic Wars.

entries.name: Third Battle of Ypres
entries.desc: Also known as Passchendaele, a WWI campaign fought by the Allies against Germany near Ypres, Belgium.

entries.name: Battle of Nagashino
entries.desc: Allied forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu decisively defeated the Takeda clan.

entries.name: Great Sioux War of 1876
entries.desc: War between the US and allied Lakota Sioux and Northern Cheyenne forces over the Black Hills.

entries.name: Arauco War
entries.desc: Long conflict between Spanish colonizers and the Mapuche people in Chile's Araucanía region.
entries.tldr: Beginning in 1546 and lasting, with intermittent truces, into the nineteenth century, the Arauco War pitted Spanish colonial forces against the Mapuche people of southern Chile, who fiercely resisted conquest of their Araucanía homeland. Mapuche warriors adapted quickly to European tactics and horses, inflicting notable defeats on the Spanish, including the death of conquistador Pedro de Valdivia in 1553. Unable to achieve lasting conquest, Spain eventually recognized the Bío-Bío River as a de facto frontier for centuries.

entries.name: Battle of White Mountain
entries.desc: Early Thirty Years' War battle near Prague where forces backing Ferdinand II defeated Frederick V's army.

entries.name: Battle of Valmy
entries.desc: France's first major Revolutionary War victory, halting a Prussian advance on Paris.

entries.name: Battle of the Golden Spurs
entries.desc: Flemish rebels won a surprise victory over the French royal army near Kortrijk in 1302.

entries.name: Siege of Yorktown
entries.desc: Final major land battle of the American Revolutionary War, won by American and French forces.

entries.name: Franco-Prussian War
entries.desc: Conflict between France and the Prussian-led North German Confederation, 1870–71.

entries.name: Svalbard Treaty
entries.desc: Recognized Norwegian sovereignty over the Svalbard archipelago while restricting its military use.

entries.name: November Uprising
entries.desc: Armed rebellion by Polish officers in Warsaw against Russian imperial rule, 1830–31.

entries.name: Entente Cordiale
entries.desc: Agreements signed in 1904 that markedly improved relations between the UK and France.

entries.name: Battle of Balaclava
entries.desc: Crimean War battle near Sevastopol between British, French, and Ottoman allies and Russian forces.
entries.tldr: Fought on 25 October 1854 during the Crimean War, the battle near the British port of Balaclava is best remembered for the disastrous Charge of the Light Brigade, in which a garbled order sent British cavalry directly into well-defended Russian guns. Earlier in the same fight, Scottish infantry famously formed a thin red line and repelled a Russian cavalry charge. Tactically inconclusive, the battle left the ongoing siege of nearby Sevastopol largely unaffected, but the Light Brigade's charge became legend, memorialized soon after in Tennyson's poem.

entries.name: Battle of Wagram
entries.desc: Napoleon's costly but decisive victory over Austria that broke up the Fifth Coalition.

entries.name: First Barbary War
entries.desc: The US fought Ottoman Tripolitania over tribute demands for safe passage of American shipping.

entries.name: Battle of Suomussalmi
entries.desc: Finnish forces defeated a much larger Soviet army during the Winter War of 1939–40.

entries.name: Battle of Kulm
entries.desc: The Battle of Kulm was fought near the town Kulm and the village Přestanov in northern Bohemia. It was fought on 29–30 August 1813, during the War of the Sixth Coalition.

entries.name: Battle of Waterloo
entries.desc: On 18 June 1815, Anglo-allied forces under Wellington and Prussian forces under Blücher defeated Napoleon near Waterloo, ending his rule permanently and bringing the Napoleonic Wars to a close.

entries.name: Battle of Badr
entries.desc: Fought on 13 March 624 CE near Badr in the Hejaz, this battle saw a small Muslim force under Muhammad defeat a larger Meccan army. The unexpected victory established Muhammad's authority and is commemorated in the Quran.
entries.tldr: Fought on 13 March 624 CE near Badr in the Hejaz, the battle saw a Muslim force of roughly 300 men led by the Prophet Muhammad ambush and rout a much larger Meccan caravan-guard army. Despite being heavily outnumbered, the Muslims used disciplined tactics and surprise to kill or capture many of Mecca's leading men, including the prominent opponent Abu Jahl. The unexpected victory sharply boosted Muhammad's authority in Medina and is referenced directly in the Quran as a sign of divine support, setting the stage for years of conflict with Mecca that followed.

entries.name: Battle of Uhud
entries.desc: The Battle of Uhud was fought between the early Muslims and the Quraysh during the Muslim–Quraysh wars in a valley north of Medina near Mount Uhud on Saturday, 23 March 625 AD.

entries.name: 1948 Arab–Israeli War
entries.desc: The interstate phase of the 1948 Palestine war, fought between Israel and neighboring Arab states after Israel declared independence. Israel won, gaining more land than the UN partition plan had proposed.
entries.tldr: When Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, armies from Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Iraq, and Lebanon invaded, opening the interstate phase of the wider 1948 Palestine war. Israeli forces, better organized despite an international arms embargo, halted the invasions and went on the offensive. Armistice agreements in 1949 left Israel controlling more territory than the 1947 UN partition plan had allotted, while Jordan and Egypt held the West Bank and Gaza. The war produced hundreds of thousands of Palestinian refugees.

entries.name: 1948 Palestine war
entries.desc: Civil war between Palestine's Arab and Jewish communities after the UN partition vote, ending with British withdrawal and Israeli independence. It caused Palestinian displacement and led into the wider Arab–Israeli war.
entries.tldr: Following the UN's November 1947 vote to partition Mandatory Palestine, fighting broke out between Arab and Jewish communities even before British forces completed their withdrawal. Jewish militias gradually gained the upper hand over Palestinian Arab irregulars and allied volunteers, capturing key cities as British administration collapsed.
